title: Europe’s Ultra-Rich Could Fund a Substantial Part of the EU’s Budget
excerpt: Taxes on wealth, crypto and financial trades could raise billions no single member state can collect alone.
content_html:
• A budget financed by wages: Gross national income-based national contributions rest largely on taxes on labour and consumption, so the EU budget ultimately leans on ordinary earners.
  • The net-position trap: While Brussels depends on national transfers, the debate collapses into who pays in and who takes out, crowding out any discussion of European public goods.
  • Taxing the very wealthy: A minimum tax on individuals with net wealth above €100 million carries by far the largest revenue potential of the options assessed.
  • Mobility argues for Europe: Financial trades, crypto assets and flights cross borders too easily for national taxation to bite, which is precisely why EU-level levies would work better.
  • New money, not recycled money: Taxes on ultra-high wealth and crypto transactions barely exist nationally, so an EU levy would add revenue rather than take it from national treasuries.

Spending needs for the EU budget for 2028–2034 have grown, and nowhere more so than in the investment required for the social and ecological transformation. At the same time, it is important to move beyond the problematic debate about higher national contributions to the EU budget, since those contributions are financed largely through taxes on labour and consumption. We have analysed how new EU revenue sources — among them taxes on ultra-high wealth and on crypto transactions — could help to do exactly that.

Political negotiations on the EU budget for the years 2028–2034 are entering a critical phase. The European Commission has presented a concrete proposal for a larger EU budget. Under it, the budget for the 2028–2034 period would amount to almost €2 trillion, or around 1.26 per cent of the EU’s gross national income (GNI), compared with approximately 1.1 per cent under the current financial framework.

The larger budget is intended to address growing public spending requirements related to climate action and digitalisation, public security and competitiveness, while also meeting the repayment obligations arising from the Covid-19 recovery fund.

The EU budget is currently financed predominantly through contributions from the member states, calculated on the basis of GNI and raised, in turn, mainly through taxes on labour and consumption. They are supplemented by revenue from value-added tax and customs duties.

Progressive Thinking on the Big Issues of Our Time

Read by policymakers, academics and journalists in 100+ countries.

This financing architecture has long been criticised, because it frequently narrows political debate to national net positions. Attention then fixes on how much each member state contributes and how much EU funding it receives in return. Such a perspective makes it more difficult to view the EU budget as an instrument for financing common European tasks, and it thereby limits the political scope for collective action at the European level.

Expanding genuine EU own resources — that is, revenue that does not come directly from national budget contributions but rests on common European levies or cross-border tax bases and is permanently assigned to the EU budget — could partly break with this logic. On the one hand, the Commission’s proposal for the 2028–2034 EU budget includes channelling 30 per cent of the revenue from the Emissions Trading System (ETS) and three-quarters of future revenue from the Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM) into the EU budget. On the other hand, it includes a levy on uncollected electronic waste, a European tobacco tax and a new corporate contribution. Together with adjustments to existing own resources — such as reducing the share of customs revenue retained by member states and increasing the plastic levy — these measures are intended to generate an additional €58.2 billion in annual revenue.

The plans presented by the European Commission have, however, already encountered reservations in several member states. It therefore makes sense to consider options that go beyond the Commission’s current proposals.

Untapped revenue potential

Our study assesses both the own resources proposed by the European Commission and a range of alternative options, evaluating them according to criteria that include their European dimension, their distributional effects, their suitability for addressing environmental and societal externalities, and their revenue potential.

The results show that various alternative instruments — among them a financial transaction tax, an EU-level digital tax, taxes on cryptocurrency transactions and online gambling, aviation-related levies, and taxes on very wealthy individuals — could generate revenue while simultaneously addressing challenges such as tax avoidance, financial-market instability, climate change and rising inequality.

The sums involved vary widely. At the modest end sit annual revenues of around €2 billion from taxing online gambling and €3 billion from levies on cryptocurrency transactions. Aviation-related taxes occupy the middle ground, at between €5 billion and €7 billion a year. At the top end, taxing ultra-wealthy individuals could raise as much as €41 billion annually.

Where only Europe can act

A financial transaction tax would not only generate additional revenue for the EU budget; it would also make short-term and speculative trading in financial markets more expensive. It could therefore help to curb certain forms of destabilising financial-market activity. Since financial transactions frequently take place across borders, and market participants can relocate relatively easily, there is a strong case for a coordinated European solution rather than fragmented national approaches. Previous proposals for a European financial transaction tax envisaged, for example, low tax rates on transactions involving shares, bonds and derivatives.

An aviation-related levy is another natural candidate for a new EU own resource. Aviation benefits from preferential tax treatment compared with other transport sectors, including exemptions from value-added tax and the limited inclusion of international flights in carbon pricing. A levy linked to the carbon dioxide emissions generated by flights could therefore reflect environmental externalities more accurately in ticket prices while simultaneously generating revenue for European priorities. Since emissions from international flights cannot meaningfully be attributed to a single member state, and national ticket taxes can partly be circumvented by flying from airports in neighbouring countries, an EU-wide solution would be best.

The taxation of crypto-assets could also be considered as a new source of revenue for the EU budget. Here the European Commission is discussing in particular a tax on crypto transactions or, alternatively, a tax on capital gains from crypto-assets. Two caveats must be taken into account: the tax base for crypto-assets fluctuates, and activities could relatively easily be relocated to jurisdictions outside the EU. This is precisely why a coordinated European solution would be preferable to a patchwork of separate national measures.

A tax on ultra-high wealth would have particularly high revenue potential. One possible approach would be a minimum tax for individuals with net wealth exceeding €100 million, ensuring that the taxes paid annually by this group amount to at least a specified proportion of their wealth. Such a tax would specifically target individuals whose effective tax burden is lower than that of other groups. At the same time, it could help to limit tax competition between member states for particularly wealthy residents.

Increasing the EU budget’s dependence on GNI-based national contributions, which rely heavily on taxes on labour income and consumption, risks undermining public support. A more developed system of genuine EU own resources could help to reorient the debate away from higher national contributions and towards the financing of European public goods and common political priorities. An agreement on additional own resources is essential if the proposed expansion of the EU budget is to be financially and politically sustainable.

Taxes on particularly mobile tax bases appear especially suitable for implementation at the EU level, since national approaches are often less effective in the face of tax competition and cross-border mobility. Some proposals — such as taxes on ultra-high wealth or on crypto-asset transactions — are particularly attractive because they currently do not exist at the national level and could therefore strengthen EU revenue without reducing any existing national tax revenue.

A better mix of own resources could strengthen the EU budget while distributing its financing more evenly across different parts of the economy, including between businesses and households.

sentences.zh: 金融交易税不仅会为欧盟预算带来额外收入，而且还会为欧盟带来更多收入。它还将使金融市场的短期和投机交易变得更加昂贵。

sentences.en: It could therefore help to curb certain forms of destabilising financial-market activity.
sentences.zh: 因此，它可能有助于遏制某些形式的破坏金融市场稳定的活动。

sentences.en: Since financial transactions frequently take place across borders, and market participants can relocate relatively easily, there is a strong case for a coordinated European solution rather than fragmented national approaches.
sentences.zh: 由于金融交易经常跨境发生，而且市场参与者可以相对容易地重新安置，因此有充分理由采取协调一致的欧洲解决方案，而不是分散的国家方案。

blocks.html_en: An aviation-related levy is another natural candidate for a new EU own resource. Aviation benefits from preferential tax treatment compared with other transport sectors, including exemptions from value-added tax and the limited inclusion of international flights in carbon pricing. A levy linked to the carbon dioxide emissions generated by flights could therefore reflect environmental externalities more accurately in ticket prices while simultaneously generating revenue for European priorities. Since emissions from international flights cannot meaningfully be attributed to a single member state, and national ticket taxes can partly be circumvented by flying from airports in neighbouring countries, an EU-wide solution would be best.

blocks.html_en: The taxation of crypto-assets could also be considered as a new source of revenue for the EU budget. Here the European Commission is discussing in particular a tax on crypto transactions or, alternatively, a tax on capital gains from crypto-assets. Two caveats must be taken into account: the tax base for crypto-assets fluctuates, and activities could relatively easily be relocated to jurisdictions outside the EU. This is precisely why a coordinated European solution would be preferable to a patchwork of separate national measures.

blocks.html_en: A tax on ultra-high wealth would have particularly high revenue potential. One possible approach would be a minimum tax for individuals with net wealth exceeding €100 million, ensuring that the taxes paid annually by this group amount to at least a specified proportion of their wealth. Such a tax would specifically target individuals whose effective tax burden is lower than that of other groups. At the same time, it could help to limit tax competition between member states for particularly wealthy residents.

sentences.en: A tax on ultra-high wealth would have particularly high revenue potential.
sentences.zh: 对超高财富征税将具有特别高的收入潜力。

blocks.html_en: Increasing the EU budget’s dependence on GNI-based national contributions, which rely heavily on taxes on labour income and consumption, risks undermining public support. A more developed system of genuine EU own resources could help to reorient the debate away from higher national contributions and towards the financing of European public goods and common political priorities. An agreement on additional own resources is essential if the proposed expansion of the EU budget is to be financially and politically sustainable.

sentences.en: A more developed system of genuine EU own resources could help to reorient the debate away from higher national contributions and towards the financing of European public goods and common political priorities.
sentences.zh: 一个更发达的真正的欧盟自有资源体系可能有助于将争论从更高的国家贡献转向欧洲公共产品和共同政治优先事项的融资。

sentences.en: An agreement on additional own resources is essential if the proposed expansion of the EU budget is to be financially and politically sustainable.
sentences.zh: 如果欧盟预算的拟议扩张要在财政和政治上可持续，就额外自有资源达成协议至关重要。

blocks.html_en: Taxes on particularly mobile tax bases appear especially suitable for implementation at the EU level, since national approaches are often less effective in the face of tax competition and cross-border mobility. Some proposals — such as taxes on ultra-high wealth or on crypto-asset transactions — are particularly attractive because they currently do not exist at the national level and could therefore strengthen EU revenue without reducing any existing national tax revenue.

sentences.zh: 针对特别流动税基的税收似乎特别适合在欧盟层面实施，因为面对税收竞争和跨境流动，国家方法往往效果较差。

sentences.en: Some proposals — such as taxes on ultra-high wealth or on crypto-asset transactions — are particularly attractive because they currently do not exist at the national level and could therefore strengthen EU revenue without reducing any existing national tax revenue.
sentences.zh: 一些提议——例如对超高财富或加密资产交易征税——特别有吸引力，因为它们目前在国家层面上并不存在，因此可以在不减少任何现有国家税收收入的情况下增加欧盟收入。

blocks.html_en: A better mix of own resources could strengthen the EU budget while distributing its financing more evenly across different parts of the economy, including between businesses and households.

sentences.en: A better mix of own resources could strengthen the EU budget while distributing its financing more evenly across different parts of the economy, including between businesses and households.
sentences.zh: 更好地组合自身资源可以加强欧盟预算，同时在经济的不同部分（包括企业和家庭之间）更均匀地分配融资。

content_html_zh:
• 由工资资助的预算：基于国民总收入的国家贡献主要依赖于劳动力税和消费税，因此欧盟预算最终依赖于普通收入者。
  • 净头寸陷阱：虽然布鲁塞尔依赖于国家转移支付，但争论归结为谁支付和谁支付，从而排除了有关欧洲公共产品的任何讨论。
  • 对非常富有的人征税：对净财富超过 1 亿欧元的个人征收最低税，是迄今为止评估的选项中最大的收入潜力。
  • 流动性为欧洲辩护：金融交易、加密资产和航班跨境太容易，国家税收难以承受，这正是欧盟层面的征税效果更好的原因。
  • 新资金，而不是回收资金：对超高财富和加密货币交易征税在全国范围内几乎不存在，因此欧盟征税将增加收入，而不是从国库中夺走收入。

2028-2034年欧盟预算的支出需求不断增长，其中社会和生态转型所需的投资增长最为明显。 与此同时，重要的是要超越关于增加国家对欧盟预算捐款的有问题的争论，因为这些捐款主要是通过劳动力税和消费税提供资金的。 我们分析了欧盟的新收入来源（其中包括对超高财富和加密货币交易征税）如何帮助实现这一目标。

关于欧盟2028-2034年预算的政治谈判正进入关键阶段。 欧盟委员会提出了一项扩大欧盟预算的具体提案。 根据该计划，2028-2034年期间的预算将达到近2万亿欧元，约占欧盟国民总收入（GNI）的1.26%，而当前财务框架下的预算约为1.1%。

更大的预算旨在满足与气候行动和数字化、公共安全和竞争力相关的日益增长的公共支出需求，同时还满足 Covid-19 复苏基金产生的还款义务。

目前，欧盟预算的资金主要来自成员国的缴款，按国民总收入计算，并主要通过劳动力税和消费税筹集。 它们还得到增值税和关税收入的补充。

对我们这个时代重大问题的进步思考

100 多个国家的政策制定者、学者和记者都在阅读。

这种融资架构长期以来一直受到批评，因为它经常将政治辩论缩小到国家净头寸。 然后注意力集中在每个成员国贡献了多少以及它收到多少欧盟资金作为回报。 这种观点使得人们更难将欧盟预算视为欧洲共同任务的融资工具，从而限制了欧洲层面集体行动的政治范围。

扩大欧盟真正的自有资源——也就是说，收入并非直接来自国家预算缴款，而是依靠欧洲共同征税或跨境税基并永久分配给欧盟预算——可能会部分打破这一逻辑。 一方面，欧盟委员会关于2028-2034年欧盟预算的提议包括将排放交易体系（ETS）收入的30％和碳边界调整机制（CBAM）未来收入的四分之三纳入欧盟预算。 另一方面，它包括对未收集的电子废物征税、欧洲烟草税和新的企业捐款。 加上对现有自身资源的调整——例如减少成员国保留的海关收入份额和增加塑料税——这些措施旨在额外产生 582 亿欧元的年收入。

然而，欧盟委员会提出的计划已经遭到一些成员国的保留。 因此，考虑超出委员会当前提案的选项是有意义的。

未开发的收入潜力

我们的研究评估了欧盟委员会提出的自身资源和一系列替代方案，根据包括其欧洲维度、分配效应、解决环境和社会外部性的适合性以及收入潜力在内的标准对其进行评估。

结果显示，各种替代工具——其中包括金融交易税、欧盟层面的数字税、加密货币交易税和在线赌博税、航空相关税以及对非常富有的个人征税——可以产生收入，同时解决避税、金融市场不稳定、气候变化和不平等加剧等挑战。

涉及的金额差异很大。 网络博彩税的年收入约为 20 亿欧元，加密货币交易税的年收入约为 30 亿欧元。 航空相关税收处于中间地带，每年 50 亿至 70 亿欧元。 在最高端，对超级富豪征税每年可以筹集高达 410 亿欧元的资金。

只有欧洲才能采取行动

金融交易税不仅会为欧盟预算带来额外收入，而且还会为欧盟带来更多收入。它还将使金融市场的短期和投机交易变得更加昂贵。 因此，它可能有助于遏制某些形式的破坏金融市场稳定的活动。 由于金融交易经常跨境发生，而且市场参与者可以相对容易地重新安置，因此有充分理由采取协调一致的欧洲解决方案，而不是分散的国家方案。 此前关于欧洲金融交易税的提议设想，例如对涉及股票、债券和衍生品的交易实行低税率。

与航空相关的税收是欧盟自身新资源的另一个自然候选者。 与其他运输部门相比，航空业受益于税收优惠，包括免除增值税以及有限地将国际航班纳入碳定价。 因此，与航班产生的二氧化碳排放挂钩的征税可以在机票价格中更准确地反映环境外部性，同时为欧洲优先事项创造收入。 由于国际航班的排放不能有意义地归因于单个成员国，而且从邻国机场起飞的航班可以部分规避国家机票税，因此欧盟范围内的解决方案将是最好的。

对加密资产征税也可以被视为欧盟预算的新收入来源。 欧盟委员会正在特别讨论对加密交易征税，或者对加密资产的资本利得征税。 必须考虑两个注意事项：加密资产的税基波动，并且活动可以相对容易地转移到欧盟以外的司法管辖区。 这正是为什么协调一致的欧洲解决方案比拼凑出单独的国家措施更可取的原因。

对超高财富征税将具有特别高的收入潜力。 一种可能的方法是对净财富超过 1 亿欧元的个人征收最低税，确保该群体每年缴纳的税款至少达到其财富的特定比例。 这种税收将专门针对有效税负低于其他群体的个人。 与此同时，它可能有助于限制成员国之间针对特别富裕居民的税收竞争。

欧盟预算越来越依赖基于国民总收入的国家缴款，而这种缴款严重依赖于对劳动收入和消费征税，这可能会削弱公众的支持。 一个更发达的真正的欧盟自有资源体系可能有助于将争论从更高的国家贡献转向欧洲公共产品和共同政治优先事项的融资。 如果欧盟预算的拟议扩张要在财政和政治上可持续，就额外自有资源达成协议至关重要。

针对特别流动税基的税收似乎特别适合在欧盟层面实施，因为面对税收竞争和跨境流动，国家方法往往效果较差。 一些提议——例如对超高财富或加密资产交易征税——特别有吸引力，因为它们目前在国家层面上并不存在，因此可以在不减少任何现有国家税收收入的情况下增加欧盟收入。

更好地组合自身资源可以加强欧盟预算，同时在经济的不同部分（包括企业和家庭之间）更均匀地分配融资。
